clue.text: Upset with sharp pain, something done with needle?

blocks.note: upset in the sense of annoyed or angry
a stitch is a sudden sharp pain in the side, often from running

explanation.surface: Someone flinches at the jab of a needle, perhaps a nervous patient at an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: The needle suggests a jab from a doctor, but it is a sewing needle; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Embroidery stitches formed as small Xs are made by hand with a threaded needle, so this is one thing produced that way.

clue.text: Animal with horn, I gathered

indicators.note: things gathered up are collected together into a fresh bundle, so the letters are regrouped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reports, as if from hearsay, that a certain beast carries a horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gathered' reads as 'I understand', but 'I' is fodder and 'gathered' the signal; the horn in the surface is also a fair hint at the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is a large thick-skinned African or Asian mammal, a straightforward example of the general category.

clue.text: Vet drops in on spook

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so these letters are left out of the word

blocks.note: to vet is to check over or examine
the letters removed, taken as written
RE means 'on the subject of', as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A veterinarian pays a casual visit to a spy, 'spook' being slang for an intelligence agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops in on' looks like one phrase meaning visits; split it after 'in', so 'drops' acts on the word before it. RE is crossword shorthand for 'on the subject of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal or literary names for a ghost or phantom that haunts a place.

clue.text: Song won’t end in joy

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that last one is kept

blocks.note: shan't is an old-fashioned equivalent of won't
the final letter of joy

explanation.surface: A sad tune that refuses to resolve into a happy ending.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAN'T and won't both mean 'will not'; the apostrophe is ignored in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a traditional work tune sung by sailors while hauling ropes, so it is one kind of song.

clue.text: Amateurish batting performance at first: strive to rein it in

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter, so only the initial is used
reining something in holds it back within limits, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: a batting side in cricket is 'in'
to exert oneself is to strive
the first letter of performance

explanation.surface: A clumsy innings by a cricketer who needs to hold back early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batting performance' reads as one phrase meaning an innings, but 'batting' alone gives IN and 'performance at first' gives P. In cricket the side batting is said to be 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking skill or experience produces work that looks unprofessional, the quality both words describe.

clue.text: Red borders trimmed with blue

indicators.note: a trim runs around the edge of something, so one piece is edged all round by the other

blocks.note: rims are edges or borders
blue is the colour of the UK Conservatives, abbreviated CON

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's note: red edging finished off with blue piping.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all colours, but 'blue' is political: blue is the Conservative Party's colour in Britain, and CON its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep, rich shade within the range of reds, so it names one particular tone of that colour.

clue.text: In top gear, as might be an assassin?

blocks.note: first meaning: wearing one's smartest, most striking clothes
second meaning, taken literally: kitted out for a murder

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top gear' suggests driving fast, but gear here is clothing. The question mark warns that the second half takes the idiom literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone glamorously turned out in eye-catching clothes, while literally it describes a hit man equipped for a job.

clue.text: Great fiddler, unbeliever in Italy

blocks.note: a pagan holds no mainstream religious belief
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A celebrated fraudster turns out to be an atheist living in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddler' suggests a swindler, but it is a violinist. 'In Italy' reads as a location, yet both words supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was the legendary Italian violin virtuoso of the early nineteenth century; fiddle is an informal name for the violin.

clue.text: Advertiser offering snack and regular meals?

blocks.note: a quick light meal between slices of bread
board is food provided daily, as in 'bed and board'

explanation.surface: A café promotes its snacks and set daily meals.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a café advertising food; really the snack and the meals are the two halves of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of placards hung front and back on a person walking the street is a means of advertising something to passers-by.

clue.text: Set up streaks for the audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the words are taken by their sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: rays are streaks of light

explanation.surface: Stage lighting beams are arranged for spectators at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like rigging stage lights for a show; the audience is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect something, such as a tent or a monument, is to put it upright in position.

clue.text: Maine car customised, a collection from there, say?

indicators.note: a customised vehicle has been altered and rebuilt to taste, so the letters are rebuilt too

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hot rod from Maine, one item in a museum of US memorabilia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' points back to Maine, a US state, and 'say' signals that the car is just one example of such items.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers artefacts and memorabilia typical of the United States and its culture, gathered as a set.

clue.text: Position of US player in two garments

blocks.note: first garment: short trousers
second garment: a shirt or blouse

explanation.surface: An American athlete is described as wearing two items of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two garments' supplies both halves: a pair of short trousers then an upper-body item.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball, the fielder stationed between second and third base occupies this spot on the diamond.

clue.text: Bear, erect

blocks.note: first meaning: tolerate, as in 'I can't bear it'
second meaning: set upright, as in putting a ladder against a wall

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a grizzly rearing up on its hind legs, but both words are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both putting up with something unpleasant and placing an object upright in position.

clue.text: Festival when consumer scoffs last of chocolates

indicators.note: to scoff is to gobble food down, so one piece swallows the other
the last of a word is its final letter, the only one taken

blocks.note: someone who consumes food
the final letter of chocolates

explanation.surface: The holiday when a greedy person polishes off the remaining chocolates.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoff is British slang for eating greedily. The chocolate eggs make the surface fit the season neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian feast celebrating the Resurrection, an annual religious holiday in spring.

clue.text: Valid fight, hollow for musician

blocks.note: a sound argument is valid
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A justified quarrel turns out empty for a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow' looks like an adjective meaning empty, but it is a noun: a cavity.
explanation.definitionFit: The resonating chamber in a guitar or violin body is an empty cavity that amplifies the strings for the player.

clue.text: Wild bird is in Italian city

indicators.note: something wild is unruly and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild bird has turned up in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild bird' looks like a single noun phrase, but 'Wild' is the signal and 'bird is in' the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Brindisi is a port on the Adriatic coast of Apulia in southern Italy, an example of the category.

clue.text: English poet using grill?

blocks.note: first meaning: Robert or Elizabeth Barrett, Victorian poets
second meaning: what a grill does to food, colouring it

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'using grill' describes the action loosely rather than giving a strict synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning wrote dramatic monologues; separately, toasting food under heat turns its surface golden-dark.

clue.text: Affectionate type in theory completely gutted, seeing hooliganism

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other
gutting removes all the innards, so only the outer shell of letters survives

blocks.note: someone who readily hugs
the outer letters of theory

explanation.surface: A tender soul is devastated on witnessing violent rowdiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' is British slang for bitterly disappointed, which disguises the cryptic sense of removing the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooligans and thugs both engage in violent, rowdy behaviour, so the two abstract nouns are close synonyms.

clue.text: Secret police try to conceal doctored tapes

indicators.note: doctored material has been tampered with and altered, so the letters are rearranged
concealing something means hiding it inside, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to have a go is to have a try
taken as written

explanation.surface: Security agents attempt a cover-up involving tampered recordings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is a noun here: a go, as in 'have a go'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was Nazi Germany's notorious state political force operating covertly against opponents.

clue.text: Concerned with swimmers, cold

blocks.note: of means about or concerning, as in 'tales of the sea'
fish are swimmers

explanation.surface: Someone worried about people in the pool, who are chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmers' suggests people in a pool; here they are aquatic creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: An offish person is distant and unfriendly in manner, which is how a cold, aloof person behaves.

clue.text: Lot of money assigned to musical composition

blocks.note: something for someone is assigned to them
a tune is a melody or short piece

explanation.surface: A large sum is earmarked for a new piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as funding a commission; 'assigned to' and the composition are simply laid end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune is a very large amount of wealth, as in 'it cost a fortune'.

clue.text: Trendily urban setter, misguided

indicators.note: misguided means led astray, so the letters are steered into a wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler, trying to sound cool and hip, has got it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like a self-reference by the compiler, but it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes fashionable city youth culture, as in 'street cred' or 'street style'.

clue.text: Incomplete sudoku surprisingly will bring praise

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing its end, so a final letter is dropped
a surprising result is an unexpected one, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: the number puzzle with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: Leaving a number puzzle unfinished somehow earns you compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's paradox is a cheeky joke; drop the final U and the five remaining letters rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos means honour, acclaim or credit given for an achievement, which is what admiring words express.

clue.text: Defeat almost catching people out, initially, in sport

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is lost
initially means at the start, so just the opening letters are taken
to catch something is to take hold of it, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: Waterloo, Napoleon's last battle, is a byword for final defeat; trimmed by one letter
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A team nearly loses at cricket despite getting batsmen out early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet one's Waterloo' means suffer a final defeat, after Napoleon's last battle in 1815.
explanation.definitionFit: Water polo is a team ball game played by swimmers in a pool, an example of a sport.

clue.text: Beat off party

blocks.note: off and out both mean not on or not working, as a light switched off
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat off' looks like a phrasal verb meaning repel, but 'Beat' is the definition alone. A do is British informal for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or perform better than a rival is to get the better of them in a contest.

clue.text: Hey, vodka’s back: fancy double?

indicators.note: the back of a word is its tail end, so just its final letter is kept

blocks.note: 'Look!' is an exclamation to get attention, like 'Hey!'
the last letter of vodka
to fancy something is to like it

explanation.surface: A drinker greets the return of vodka and offers a double measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' is a bar order for a double measure, but here it means a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who closely resembles someone else, such as a celebrity, is called their double.

clue.text: Total, say

blocks.note: first meaning: complete, absolute
second meaning: to speak or pronounce words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' usually signals an example, but here it is a plain verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means complete or absolute; as a verb it means to voice or articulate words.

clue.text: Flower shape, people inspired by little one

indicators.note: to be inspired is literally to be breathed in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to forge metal is to shape it
a tot is a small child
men are people

explanation.surface: A form of bloom, or folk motivated by a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspired by' reads as 'motivated by'; take it literally as drawn inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The forget-me-not is a small plant with sky-blue blossoms, a classic example of the general category.
